title: JUDGMENT
key_sentences: The Claimant says that 1,240 tonnes of wheat were rejected by its buyer because they had become infested and damp while in the Defendant’s custody.
The Defendant accepts that it stored the wheat but denies that the damage occurred while the wheat was in its warehouse.
On 2 June 2025 the Claimant’s buyer sent a surveyor to sample the wheat before collection.
A bailee for reward must show that it took reasonable care of the goods, or that its failure to do so did not cause the loss.
The Defendant’s expert suggested that the weevils could have been present at delivery in numbers too small to detect.
The Claimant argues that the clause was not incorporated, because the standard terms were first sent after the storage contract had been concluded.
In my judgment, a reference of that kind is sufficient to incorporate standard terms between commercial parties of equal bargaining power.
I will hear the parties on interest and costs if they cannot agree them within 14 days of the hand-down of this judgment.

list_items.text: (a) whether the wheat was damaged while it was in the Defendant’s custody; and
(b) if it was, whether clause 14 limits the Defendant’s liability.
